# Checkmate Dynamics: full site text

> Checkmate Dynamics is a Dallas robotics and drone hardware company. It makes motion nodes, actuators and cycloidal gearboxes, sensors such as the Contour lidar, and hubs, for robot arms and robot training-data rigs; a flight-sensor node for drones is in development. Everything works together out of the box. Makers use the nodes one at a time, robotics companies build them in, and our data-station hardware is assembled from them. Prices are list prices in US dollars.

Specifications are datasheet figures, values set by our design, or bench measurements. Prices are list prices in USD. Legal notices and pre-order terms: https://checkmatedynamics.com/legal.md. Every page has a markdown version at the same address ending in .md.

---

**03** System

## One cable per device.

Each node’s own USB-C port is the bus: power negotiated over PD, USB to a computer, and CAN to everything else. On a bench, a phone charger runs one node. On a floor, a Hub 8 Pro runs eight.

|  |  |  |  |  |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | SmartStepper 17 |  | USB-C, PD + USB + CAN 1 Mbit/s |  |
| A2 | SmartServo G × n |  | USB-C, CAN-FD |  |
| B1 | Contour |  | USB-C, depth and sync in |  |
| C1 | Sync Beacon |  | USB-C, station clock |  |
| D1 | Hub 8 Pro |  | 8 node ports with PD per port, 2 accessory ports, CAN star with isolated ports, 20 V motor rail, E-stop in |  |
| PC | Host PC |  | One USB device. Python SDK, ROS 2, LeRobot, MCAP |  |

Fig. 02 — Bus topology. Hub 8 Pro ports are point-to-point segments, so a damaged cable is cut off without stopping the others.

**04** Test card

## Every unit ships with its own numbers.

Each node is calibrated and measured at final test, and the results go in the box and stay on the node. We publish measured values.

- Encoder calibration stored on the node, not in a laptop’s config file
- Backlash, backdrive and torque recorded per serial number
- The same record goes to makers, OEM customers and our own stations

**Unit test card** SmartServo G-2804 · 20:1

Serial | CM-A23-000127

Encoder calibration | 16,384 counts/turn | at test

Backlash, output | 4.6 arcmin | at test

Backdrive, unpowered | 0.21 N·m | at test

Continuous torque, 20 V | 0.93 N·m | at test

Thermal soak, 30 min | 41 °C | at test

PD contract | 20 V | at test

Each unit’s values are measured at final test. | Dallas, TX

# One family of nodes.

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/products.html

Products | Four families · one bus

Every product is a finished unit that works on its own and joins the same USB-C bus as the rest. Learn one and you know the next: same cable, same status light, same app.

**A** Move

## Motor nodes with everything inside.

Driver, encoder, controller and gearbox built in and calibrated as one unit. Reducers are part of the nodes, not separate parts.

**A1** SmartStepper 17 From $79

Closed-loop NEMA 17. Board, direct-drive node, or with a 25:1 metal cycloidal.

**A2** SmartServo G From $89

Brushless servo for 2804 and 5208 gimbal motors, direct drive or cycloidal. The Leader’s joints.

**B** Sense

## The scene around the robot, the angle inside the joint.

Contour | **54 × 42 zones**

Wireframe from CAD

**B1–B2** Contour, Contour Wrist Contour $349

Metric time-of-flight depth over USB-C, synced to your cameras. The Wrist version rides on the gripper.

**B3** Output encoder $29

Reads a reducer’s output angle directly. Standard on geared nodes, sold for retrofit.

**C** Sync

## An instrument for the station.

The Sync Beacon doesn’t measure the scene or a joint. It is a clock your cameras film, so every stream can be placed on one timeline and checked against the others. That’s why it has a family of its own.

[Sync Beacon](https://checkmatedynamics.com/sync-beacon.html)

A 14-day timing check is $1,250 per station; owning a beacon is $999. Patent pending.

**Station Report** episode 000127

Drift, session | 0.40 ms/h | Pass

Station Report | C1

# SmartStepper 17

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/smartstepper-17.html

[Products](https://checkmatedynamics.com/products.html) / A — Move / A1 | Closed-loop stepper node

A closed-loop NEMA 17 that runs on a USB-C charger and sets up in a browser. Add the 25:1 metal cycloidal and it becomes a robot joint.

**A1.1 · Board** | Controller for your own NEMA 17 | **$79**

**A1.2 · SmartStepper 17 · Direct** | Direct drive: board on a calibrated NEMA 17, housed | **$169**

**A1.3 · SmartStepper 17 · 25:1** | Cycloidal reducer and output encoder | **$279**

[Register interest](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Register%20interest%3A%20SmartStepper%2017) | [Volume / OEM](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Parts%20and%20OEM%20enquiry%3A%20SmartStepper%2017)

*Output flange · M3 bolt circle, dowels* *25:1 cycloidal · 42 mm square* *NEMA 17 · flying-lead or socketed* *Rear unit · controller, 45.3 mm square* *USB-C · PD, USB, CAN*

**Fig. 01** SmartStepper 17 · 25:1, three-quarter view

Key figures

- **Encoder**: 14-bit, 16,384 counts
- **Power**: USB-C PD, 5–20 V
- **Bus**: CAN 1 Mbit/s
- **Reduction**: 25:1 cycloidal
- **Gearbox**: 42 mm square

45.3 mm

42 mm

Plan view, to scale | Diagram

**01** Overview

## A stepper that knows where it is.

01

### Closed loop

A 14-bit magnetic encoder (16,384 counts per turn) watches the shaft, so a stall is reported instead of silently losing position.

02

### Runs on a charger

Any USB-C Power Delivery charger supplies 5 to 20 V. The same port carries USB to a laptop and CAN to the next node.

03

### Browser setup

The Checkmate app runs in your browser: calibrate, set current, jog, and plot angle, current and temperature live.

04

### Your NEMA 17 or ours

Works with flying-lead or socketed NEMA 17 motors (adapter included). The leads plug into the rear unit; closed loop needs a rear shaft for the encoder magnet.

**02** Direct drive

## The motor shaft is the output.

SmartStepper 17 · Direct is the complete node with no reducer: the same closed-loop board and calibrated NEMA 17, housed, with the shaft driving your load.

01

### Full motor speed

No gearbox between the motor and the load. For turntables, slides, fixtures and printer or CNC axes that need speed more than torque.

02

### Nothing to wear

No reducer means no backlash from gearing and no gear stage to service. The encoder watches the shaft that does the work.

03

### Geared later

The 25:1 reducer bolts to the motor face. A direct node becomes A1.3 for the price difference, and keeps its identity and calibration history.

List price $169. Direct-drive output covers and frames are in design.

**03** Reducer

## A metal cycloidal inside the motor’s own footprint.

Two cycloid discs share the load across many rollers, which keeps the joint stiff and low in backlash without growing past the 42 mm outline.

- Lost motion and torque measured on every unit and printed on its test card
- Output encoder fitted as standard
- Output face with M3 bolt circle and dowel holes

*Output carrier* *Cycloid discs × 2* *Motor body, exposed*

**Fig. 02** Quarter section of the reducer

**04** Integration

*Controller board* *NEMA 17 · flying leads*

**Fig. 03** Rear unit: magnet, frame, board, cover

## Drops into a printer, a CNC or an arm.

Drive it over CAN from Python, or take STEP/DIR from Klipper, Marlin or GRBL boards on the AUX port. To Klipper it is an ordinary external driver.

- Qwiic port for I²C sensors and displays
- AUX: STEP/DIR, endstop, UART or sync
- Chain nodes over CAN on the same cable
- An anodized aluminum Cable Clip holds the USB-C cable in place (in the box)

**05** Specification

|  | SmartStepper 17 · Direct | SmartStepper 17 · 25:1 |
|---|---|---|
| Motor | NEMA 17, pre-mounted and calibrated. Board: your own flying-lead or socketed NEMA 17 (adapter included) with a rear shaft for the encoder magnet | Same, with 25:1 metal cycloidal |
| Size | 45.3 mm square rear unit | 42 mm square gearbox · 45.3 mm square rear unit |
| Controller / driver | ESP32-S3 (USB; Wi-Fi and BLE off by default, enabled in the app) / TMC2209 | Same |
| Encoder | MT6701, 14-bit, motor shaft | Same, plus output encoder |
| Power | USB-C PD sink, 5–20 V | Same |
| Bus | CAN 1 Mbit/s on the USB-C cable | Same |
| Ports | USB-C · Qwiic · AUX 4-pin JST-SH | Same |
| Backlash | — | Measured per unit, on the test card |
| Torque | Motor-dependent, measured per unit | Measured per unit, on the test card |
| Software | Checkmate browser app · Python SDK · Klipper STEP/DIR guide |  |
| Compliance | US only at launch |  |

CAN needs a full-featured USB-C cable; charge-only cables don’t carry it. Every unit ships with its measured test card.

**06** Figures

## The node from other angles.

**Fig. 04** Output face

**Fig. 05** Rear unit, Cable Clip on USB-C

**Fig. 06** Controller board

# SmartServo G

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/smartservo-g.html

[Products](https://checkmatedynamics.com/products.html) / A — Move / A2 | Brushless gimbal-motor servo

A complete brushless actuator: gimbal motor, field-oriented control, magnetic encoder and housing, on one USB-C cable. The Checkmate Leader is built from these.

**A2.1 · Board** | One board for 2804 and 5208 motors | **$89**

**A2.2 · G-2804 · Direct** | Direct drive, no gearbox, no backlash | **$159**

**A2.3 · G-2804 · 20:1** | Cycloidal, output encoder, I/O tile | **$249**

**A2.4 · G-5208 · Direct** | Direct drive, larger motor | **$249**

**A2.5 · G-5208 · 25:1** | Cycloidal, output encoder, I/O tile | **$399**

[Register interest](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Register%20interest%3A%20SmartServo%20G) | [Volume / OEM](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Parts%20and%20OEM%20enquiry%3A%20SmartServo%20G)

*G-2804 · iFlight GBM2804H-100T* *G-5208 · iFlight GM5208, 24 winding*

**Fig. 01** SmartServo G nodes, both motor sizes

Key figures

- **Motors**: 2804 · 5208
- **Reduction**: 20:1 · 25:1
- **Encoder**: 14-bit
- **Power**: USB-C PD, 5–20 V
- **Bus**: CAN-FD
- **Torque**: Measured per unit

Ø35 mm

Controller board, to scale | Diagram

**01** Overview

## Built for feel and fidelity, not raw force.

01

### Quiet

Field-oriented control on a gimbal motor: smooth motion with no stepping and almost no sound.

02

### Absolute

A 14-bit encoder on the motor axis with calibration stored on the node. Geared versions add an output encoder.

03

### Backdrivable

Move it by hand and record the motion. Made for leader arms, wrists, grippers, camera heads and haptics.

04

### One cable

USB-C PD power and CAN-FD between nodes on the same cable. Setup runs in the Checkmate app in your browser.

Not for lifting shoulders or wheels. For those you want a higher-torque actuator, and we’ll say so.

**02** Direct drive

## No gearbox between you and the motor.

G-2804 · Direct and G-5208 · Direct are complete nodes with the gimbal motor driving your load. Both use the same board, the same cable and the same app as the geared nodes.

01

### Backdrivable

With no gear stage to fight, the shaft can be moved by hand. That is the feel haptics, knobs and hand-held controls depend on.

02

### Smooth and quiet

Field-oriented control on a gimbal motor, with no gear stage to add backlash.

03

### Test fixtures and benches

Rate tables, load stages, camera heads and teaching benches need speed and clean torque more than reduction. The G-5208 · Direct is the larger of the two.

List prices $159 and $249. Torque is measured per unit and printed on the test card. Direct-drive output covers and frames are in design.

**03** Construction

*I/O tile (optional)* *Ø35 mm controller board* *Base plate* *Gimbal motor*

**Fig. 02** The stack, 2804 version

## A round board that sits on the motor.

Controller, driver and encoder share one board on the motor’s back. The optional I/O tile stacks on top, and an aluminum cover closes it.

- STM32G431 controller, DRV8316 driver
- USB-C PD sink, capped at 20 V
- Calibration stored on the node
- Two dowels in every cap face for repeatable swaps

**04** Variants

## Two motors, direct or geared.

**A2.2–A2.3** G-2804 · Direct and G-2804 · 20:1 $159 / $249

Compact and light. Direct drive for handle roll, camera pan and haptic knobs. The 20:1 cycloidal for wrists, grippers and leader joints.

**A2.4–A2.5** G-5208 · Direct and G-5208 · 25:1 $249 / $399

Larger and stronger. Direct drive for haptics and camera heads. The 25:1 cycloidal for the heavier joints of a leader arm.

**05** Specification

|  | G-2804 · Direct | G-2804 · 20:1 | G-5208 · Direct | G-5208 · 25:1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Motor | iFlight GBM2804H-100T | iFlight GM5208, 24 winding |  |  |
| Reducer | Direct | 20:1 cycloidal | Direct | 25:1 cycloidal |
| Lost motion | 0 | Measured per unit | 0 | Measured per unit |
| Encoders | Motor, 14-bit | Motor + output | Motor, 14-bit | Motor + output |
| Torque | Measured per unit and printed on the test card; curves published after the first batch |  |  |  |
| Controller / driver | STM32G431 / DRV8316 |  |  |  |
| Power | USB-C PD sink, 5–20 V |  |  |  |
| Bus | CAN-FD on the USB-C cable; classic CAN when mixed with SmartStepper |  |  |  |
| I/O | Optional tile | Tile included | Optional tile | Tile included |
| Software | Checkmate browser app over USB (Chrome, Edge) · Python SDK · LeRobot |  |  |  |

Each unit ships with its own measured test card.

**06** Accessories

### D3 · I/O tile

Stacks on the board. Adds Qwiic and a 4-pin AUX port for sensors, endstops and triggers.

$19

Ring magnet and side sensor 3-axis

A 3-axis magnetic sensor and ring magnet in the reducer cap. Standard on geared nodes, sold for retrofit.

$29

# Contour

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/contour.html

[Products](https://checkmatedynamics.com/products.html) / B — Sense / B1–B2 | Direct time-of-flight depth

Metric depth from a sensor the size of a thumb, over one USB-C cable and on the same clock as your cameras. It measures distance directly, so plain, textureless surfaces read as well as patterned ones.

**B1 · Contour** | USB-C depth sensor | **$349**

**B2 · Contour Wrist** | Gripper mount, on the station clock | **Stations**

**Contour OEM** | Module for your own housing | **Talk to us**

[Register interest](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Register%20interest%3A%20Contour) | [OEM enquiry](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Parts%20and%20OEM%20enquiry%3A%20Contour)

Sensor figures from ST’s datasheet.

Resolution | **54 × 42 zones**

Field of view | **55° × 42°**

Frame rate | **30 Hz**

Sensor range | **0.05–8.8 m**

**Fig. 01** Contour development unit (case rev B), with the sensor’s figures Wireframe from CAD

Key figures

- **Sensor**: VL53L9CX
- **Wavelength**: 940 nm
- **Resolution**: 54 × 42
- **Frame rate**: 30 Hz
- **Size**: 46 × 41 mm
- **Interface**: USB-C

46 mm

41 mm

Front view, to scale | Diagram

**01** Overview

## Geometry at contact range.

01

### Metric

Direct time-of-flight returns absolute distance whatever the surface color or texture.

02

### Small

A 46 × 41 mm footprint, small enough to sit beside a follower arm’s gripper.

03

### On the clock

A sync input lines depth frames up with your RGB cameras and the rest of the station.

04

### In your pipeline

Appears as a camera in LeRobot, with depth and confidence for every frame.

**02** Contour Wrist

## Depth beside the gripper, next to the camera you already run.

Contour Wrist mounts on the follower’s wrist with adapters for common arms and adds contact-range depth on the station clock. It is in development alongside the [Sync Beacon](https://checkmatedynamics.com/sync-beacon.html).

- Station profile tuned for 5 cm to 1.5 m
- Per‑unit calibration file in the box
- Mounted on the follower, never the leader

Where it fits

| Lighting | Indoor, LED-lit stations |
|---|---|
| Frame rate | 30 Hz, depth + confidence |
| Resolution | 54 × 42 zones: contact geometry, not an RGB replacement |
| Not for | Direct sunlight, halogen lamps, scenes full of glass |

**03** Specification

| Sensor | ST VL53L9CX direct time-of-flight, 940 nm, Class 1 laser |
|---|---|
| Resolution | 54 × 42 zones; binned modes down to 4 × 4 |
| Field of view | 55° × 42° |
| Range | 0.05–8.8 m sensor range; 1.5 m clamp in the station profile |
| Frame rate | 30 Hz over USB, depth and confidence |
| Size | 46 × 41 mm footprint |
| Interfaces | USB-C · sync input |
| Software | LeRobot camera plugin · Python |

Sensor figures from ST’s datasheet.

For headsets, wrist rigs and handheld grippers: the Contour module with the same calibration and sync, supplied with per‑unit test records and integration support.

# Hub 8 Pro

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/hub-8.html

[Products](https://checkmatedynamics.com/products.html) / D — Power & connect / D1 | Eight-port node hub

Powers, connects and protects a whole arm of nodes. Every port is its own USB-C power source and its own CAN segment, so one damaged cable can’t take the rest down.

**D1 · Hub 8 Pro** | Hub only; power supply optional | **$399**

[Talk to us](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Parts%20and%20OEM%20enquiry%3A%20Hub%208%20Pro) | [Book a call](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Data%20station%20call%3A%20Hub%208%20Pro)

Ships inside the Checkmate Leader and on its own.

*P1–P8 · node ports, PD + CAN each* *Machined 6061 case*

**Fig. 01** Hub 8 Pro, port side

Key figures

- **Node ports**: 8 + 2 accessory
- **Port power**: 20 V / 1.5 A
- **Bus**: CAN-FD star
- **Power in**: 12–48 V DC
- **Host**: 1 × USB
- **E-stop**: 2-channel NC

218 mm

120 mm

Plan view, to scale | Diagram

**01** Overview

## A star, not a chain.

01

### Eight node ports

Plus two accessory ports for a Sync Beacon or Contour, and an upstream port to chain hubs for bimanual stations.

02

### Power per port

Each port is a USB-C PD source: off when empty, 20 V at 1.5 A once a node asks for it, and 3 A on up to two ports.

03

### Isolated CAN

Every port is its own CAN segment, bridged inside the hub. A crushed cable is cut off; the others keep running.

04

### Hardware e-stop

A two-channel input removes motor power in hardware, with no firmware in the path.

**02** Host

## One cable to the PC, one device for every node.

The hub appears as a single USB device whose CAN channels show up as standard SocketCAN interfaces on Linux. Each node’s own USB stays reachable for setup and updates.

- CAN-FD for SmartServo G, classic CAN for SmartStepper and accessories
- Shared 20 V motor rail: one node’s braking feeds another
- Per-port power and bus telemetry
- Machined aluminum case

*Power in* *E-stop · link · sync*

**Fig. 02** Rear panel

**03** Bus cable

**Fig. 03** A node’s USB-C cable held by the Cable Clip

## Power, USB and CAN on one cable.

Every Checkmate device uses its own USB-C port as the bus. Any full-featured USB-C cable carries all three; charge-only cables won’t carry CAN.

- One cable and one Cable Clip (anodized 6061) ship in every node box; extra clips $9
- The Clip Bar 8 screws across all eight ports and clamps every cable, so a snag can’t pull a joint offline

**04** Specification

| Ports | 8 node · 2 accessory · 1 upstream; USB-C with M2 threads for the Clip Bar 8 |
|---|---|
| Port power | USB-C PD source per port: 5 V on attach, 20 V / 1.5 A on request; 3 A on up to 2 ports |
| Bus | Active CAN star with CAN-FD and classic domains; ports isolated |
| Host link | One USB device per hub; SocketCAN-compatible channels |
| Safety | Two-channel normally-closed e-stop input; hardware cut of motor power |
| Power in | 12–48 V DC or USB-C PD; supply optional |
| Enclosure | Machined 6061 aluminum, 218 × 120 × 34 mm |
| Cascading | Second hub’s upstream port into an accessory port; one hub per arm |

Each shipped unit comes with its own measured test card.

# Prove your cameras agree on time.

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/sync-beacon.html

[Stations](https://checkmatedynamics.com/stations.html) / C — Sync / C1 | Timing test instrument · Patent pending

Cameras, robot joints and sensors each keep their own clock. Your training data comes out misaligned, and most rigs never measure by how much. The Sync Beacon is a clock your cameras can film. It puts every frame on one timeline, and a Station Report shows the result.

**14-day rental** | A beacon ships to you, per station | **$1,250**

**Own one** | A founding Sync Beacon, yours | **$999**

[Book a timing check](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Sync%20Beacon%20timing%20check&body=Cameras%20and%20frame%20rates%3A%0ARobot%20and%20recorder%3A%0ALocation%3A) | See the offers

A timing test instrument for rig validation and QA. Sold to labs and companies.

**Fig. 01** Sync Beacon, exterior Wireframe from CAD

**01** The problem

## Every stream on your rig keeps its own time.

Each camera, joint log and depth stream stamps its data on a different clock. When they disagree, the dataset pairs images with the wrong joint readings.

01

### Cameras stamp late

A USB camera’s timestamp is usually when the host received the frame, not when the sensor exposed it. Buffers and USB scheduling put an unknown delay between the two.

02

### Clocks start apart and drift

Joint encoders log on the controller’s clock. Cameras log on the PC’s. They start at different moments and move apart over a session.

03

### Most rigs never measure it

Without a shared reference, skew shows up as a policy that almost works and an episode that gets rejected with no stated cause. Most rigs carry no number for it.

**—** Same moment

Beacon clock

Camera A

Camera B

Wrist camera

Joint log

**Fig. 02** One instant, four clocks. The dashed line marks the same moment Diagram

**frame_index / fps**

How LeRobot computes each recorded frame’s timestamp: from the frame counter, not from the camera. It records when the recorder counted the frame, not when the camera captured it.

[LeRobot source, dataset_writer.py line 225](https://github.com/huggingface/lerobot/blob/626da71be9d21b3c740b6438514519a503a2d535/src/lerobot/datasets/dataset_writer.py#L225), read Oct 28, 2026

**02** The beacon

## A clock your cameras can film.

The beacon sits in view of your cameras and shows an LED clock that steps every 1 ms. Every camera films it. The decoder reads the clock in each frame, so every frame’s exposure time lands on one clock.

You get dropped frames, repeated frames, true frame intervals and the offset between cameras, per camera. It is built for any camera that can see it, and your Station Report confirms it on your cameras. Nothing is wired to the cameras, and nothing changes in your recorder.

**Fig. 03** The LED face: 8 × 8, stepping every 1 ms Diagram

**1 ms**

LED clock step. Selectable at 0.5 ms and 2 ms.

**8 × 8**

Green LED face, 525 nm. Green light passes the IR-cut filter on camera sensors.

**Any camera**

Built for webcams, machine-vision cameras and phones that can see the face. Your Station Report confirms each camera.

**03** Station Report

## Proof, not a feeling.

The Station Report lists, for each camera, how many frames were placed on the beacon clock, what was dropped or repeated, the true frame interval, and the offset to every other camera.

Keep it with the dataset. When a data buyer or a reviewer asks how well aligned the streams are, you have the measurement.

Accuracy on real cameras is measured for your rig in the Station Report.

**Station Report** session 03 · station B-04

Camera A, frames on beacon clock | 1,799 / 1,800

Camera A, dropped · repeated | 1 · 0

Camera B, true frame interval | 33.4 ms

Camera B, offset to camera A | +6.2 ms

Wrist camera, offset to camera A | −11.8 ms

Shutter type · line time | rolling · 18 µs

Station Report

**04** How it works

## Place it, record a minute, read the report.

01

### Place it in view

Set the beacon where every camera can see its face, on a tripod or clamp. The Station Report confirms the placement for each camera. Power from any USB port.

02

### Record a test session

Set a short manual exposure and lock focus on the face. Record every camera over the same 60 s.

03

### Decode and read

Run the decoder on each video on your PC. Every frame lands on the beacon clock, and the Station Report shows drops, repeats, intervals and camera-to-camera offset.

**05** Who it’s for

## Teams that need to know their rig is aligned.

Use it to check a rig before you record on it and again whenever the rig changes.

A

### Data-collection teams

Validate each new station before it records. Re-check after a camera swap, a USB change or a rebuild. Hand your buyer a measurement of the timing, not a promise.

B

### University labs

Know your cameras and arms line up before a study’s data collection starts, and put the figures in the methods. Invoiced by P-card, PO, card or ACH.

C

### Rig builders and integrators

Commission a station, find the camera that runs late and confirm the fix, with the same instrument on every rig you build.

Rent one for 14 days, or own one from the start.

**07** At a glance

## What it is, in numbers.

| LED clock | 1 ms step, with 0.5 ms and 2 ms selectable |
|---|---|
| LED face | 8 × 8 green LEDs, 525 nm |
| Cameras | Built for any camera that can see the face; confirmed per camera in the Station Report. No wiring to the camera |
| Reference pulses | Two SYNC outputs, 100 µs active-low pulses, 30 Hz by default |
| Clock stability | ±0.14 ppm over 3 h on the first unit measured (bench result, Oct 26, 2026). Each unit ships with its own calibration certificate |
| Power | USB-C, 5 V. No radio, no network |
| Mounting | 1/4”-20 tripod adapter |
| Decoder | Runs on your PC in Python 3 with numpy and OpenCV |

**06** Questions

**Who is Checkmate Dynamics?**

A robotics hardware company in Dallas, Texas. We design motion, sensing and sync hardware (SmartStepper, SmartServo G, Contour, the Sync Beacon and Hub 8 Pro) and build station products from it.

**What happens when something breaks?**

Every Leader joint is the same kind of node, so a repair is a swap, not a visit. Service plans include advance replacement; terms are confirmed before a plan starts.

**Do you see our data?**

No. Recordings stay on your machines and everything works on-prem. We see only the reports you choose to send us.

**Do the devices touch our network?**

No. The beacon and Contour are USB devices with no radio and no network connection. The recorder plugin runs on your PC.

**Will the beacon affect our training data?**

It should not: the beacon is a separate USB device and changes nothing on your cameras. We walk through the details on a call.

**We already sync our cameras in hardware.**

Keep it. Hardware sync ties those cameras together; the beacon checks every stream on the station, including webcams, joint logs and wrist depth, and certifies each episode.

**Can we try it first?**

Start with a Skew Audit on one station. Register your interest and we agree the details on a call.

# Perfect the nodes. Build everything else from them.

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/company.html

Company | Dallas, Texas

Checkmate Dynamics is a Dallas robotics and drone hardware company. We make motion nodes, actuators and cycloidal gearboxes, sensors such as the Contour lidar, and hubs for robot arms and robot training-data rigs, and we are developing a flight-sensor node for drones.

**01** Principles

## How we build.

01

### One family

Same cable, connector, bus, clock, app and look across every product. Own one node and you know the next.

02

### Plug in, then work

Plug it in and it’s found, named and ready. Settings exist; nobody needs them to start.

03

### Measured, not promised

We publish measurements, and every unit ships with its own test card.

04

### Value first

We aim for the best part in its class, judged by the work it saves you.

05

### Built from the same nodes

Our larger products are assemblies of the retail nodes, hub and cable. Improve one node and everything improves.

06

### Continuity

Identity, calibration and history travel with a node from a maker’s bench to a data floor.

07

### Your data is yours

Everything works on-prem; the cloud is optional. Station devices have no radio, any node radio is off until you turn it on in the app, and we never receive your recordings.

08

### Finished

Closed housings, labeled ports, and one look from the product to the box to this page.

# Build a teleoperation rig for robot training data.

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/build-a-teleoperation-rig.html

Guide | Updated November 10, 2026

A rig that records demonstrations for imitation learning needs five things: a follower arm, a leader the operator moves, two or more cameras, a recorder, and a way to check that all the streams share one clock.

**01** Answer

## The short version.

Most open rigs pair a follower arm with a small leader that has the same joint layout. The operator moves the leader and the follower copies it while the recorder saves camera frames, joint positions and actions. LeRobot and GELLO are the common open-source starting points. Pick the leader by how much feel, durability and warranty you need.

- **Follower arm:** the arm you want the policy to run on. The leader copies its joint layout.
- **Leader:** an SO-101 leader, a GELLO build, a Franka GELLO or the Checkmate Leader (below).
- **Cameras:** at least one wrist camera and one fixed view. Add Contour depth at the gripper if your policy uses it.
- **Power and connection:** one supply and bus per arm. Hub 8 Pro powers and connects up to eight Checkmate nodes over a single USB link.
- **Recorder:** LeRobot, or the SDK of your arm maker.
- **Timing check:** measure camera skew before you record, not after episodes are rejected. The [sync guide](https://checkmatedynamics.com/sync-cameras-and-joints.html) shows how.

**02** Leader options

## Four ways to build the leader.

|  | SO-101 leader | GELLO | Franka GELLO | Checkmate Leader |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Joint actuator | Feetech STS3215 serial-bus servo, $22.00 each (Seeed, read 2026-11-10) | Dynamixel XL330-M288-T, $27.49 each (ROBOTIS US, read 2026-11-10) | 7 x Dynamixel XL330-M288-T plus a trigger servo (Franka parts list, read 2026-10-09) | 8 SmartServo G nodes (G-2804 and G-5208) |
| Gravity support | Passive | Passive (3D-printed frame) | Passive: torsion springs at joints 2 and 4 | Active gravity compensation at every joint |
| Force feedback | None | None | None published | Haptic walls at joint limits; trigger force feedback |
| Availability | Parts you buy and print | Open-source design; parts you buy and print | Prototype, by quote; price on request (franka.de/gello, read 2026-11-10) | In design; $2,990 per arm, register interest |
| Fit | SO-101 and LeRobot builders | Many follower arms; Franka FR3 variant exists | Franka FR3 labs | Kinematics matched to your follower |

Competitor prices were checked on the vendors’ own pages on 2026-11-10 (see research/aeo/guide-price-check-2026-11-10.md); the Franka parts list is from research/competitor-franka-gello.md, read 2026-10-09. Prices and availability change; check the vendor. Checkmate prices are the list prices on our [Leader](https://checkmatedynamics.com/leader.html) page. Checkmate products are shown before FCC authorization; see [Legal](https://checkmatedynamics.com/legal.html#fcc).

**03** Fit

## When each one makes sense.

- **SO-101 or GELLO.** Choose these for the lowest part cost, an open design you can print and repair yourself, and a rig that follows the LeRobot community. A maker building an SO-101 follower should buy the STS3215 servos it was designed around.
- **Franka GELLO.** Choose it if you run Franka FR3 arms and want a leader from the same vendor. Franka labels it a prototype and sells it by quote.
- **Checkmate Leader.** Choose it when operators work long shifts and the arm should hold its own weight, show the follower’s limits and gripper force, and return home between episodes. Every joint is a node you can swap on its own. It is in design: no unit ships yet, and you can register interest as a design partner.

## Power and connection.

Checkmate nodes take power and CAN over one USB-C cable. [Hub 8 Pro](https://checkmatedynamics.com/hub-8.html) ($399) gives each of eight node ports its own 20 V source and its own CAN segment, plus a hardware e-stop input, and appears to the PC as one USB device.

## Cameras and depth.

Any camera that LeRobot or your recorder supports works. [Contour](https://checkmatedynamics.com/contour.html) is a 54 x 42 zone time-of-flight depth sensor (VL53L9CX, 30 Hz, 46 x 41 mm) that mounts beside the follower’s gripper and takes a sync input.

**04** Questions

**What hardware do I need for a robot teleoperation data rig?**

A follower arm, a leader arm the operator moves, at least two cameras, a recorder such as LeRobot, and a way to power and connect the joints. Add a timing check so you know the camera streams share one clock.

**What are good leader arms besides GELLO?**

The SO-101 leader from the LeRobot project, built on Feetech STS3215 servos, is the common open alternative. Franka sells a pre-assembled GELLO by quote. The Checkmate Leader, which is in design, uses active gravity compensation and force feedback and costs $2,990 per arm at list.

**Does the Checkmate Leader exist yet?**

It is in design. The nodes it uses, SmartServo G and Hub 8 Pro, are the products on this site. No Leader ships yet; labs and floors can register interest as design partners.

**Do I need a hub?**

Not for a rig built on serial-bus servos, which daisy-chain. For Checkmate nodes, Hub 8 Pro gives each port its own power and CAN segment, so one damaged cable does not take the other joints down.

Related: [Guides](https://checkmatedynamics.com/guides.html) · [Checkmate Leader](https://checkmatedynamics.com/leader.html) · [Hub 8 Pro](https://checkmatedynamics.com/hub-8.html) · [Sync Beacon](https://checkmatedynamics.com/sync-beacon.html)

# Sync cameras and joint data to one clock.

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/sync-cameras-and-joints.html

Guide | Updated November 10, 2026

There are two jobs: make the streams share a clock, and measure how far apart they still are. Hardware trigger or timecode does the first. A camera-visible clock does the second, on any camera.

**01** Answer

## Why the streams drift apart.

A USB camera’s timestamp is usually when the host received the frame, not when the sensor exposed it. Joint encoders log on the controller’s clock and cameras log on the PC’s, so the two start apart and move apart over a session.

LeRobot computes each recorded frame’s timestamp as frame_index / fps, from the frame counter and not from the camera (LeRobot dataset_writer.py, line 225, re-read on the main branch Nov 10, 2026). A dataset can therefore look aligned while the cameras are not.

## Three approaches.

- **Trigger the cameras together.** A trigger hub or GPIO cable starts every exposure at the same moment. It needs cameras with a trigger input.
- **Stamp the streams with timecode.** A timecode generator writes the same time to audio and video devices. It does not measure per-frame skew on a robot rig.
- **Measure the result.** Put a clock in view of every camera, record it, and read the clock out of each frame. This works for webcams and for hardware-synced rigs alike, and it shows what the other two approaches actually achieved.

**02** Options

## What is on the market.

| Option | What it does | List price | Limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Orbbec Sync Hub Pro | Triggers Orbbec cameras together | $70 to $76 at US resellers; Orbbec publishes no list price (Knoxlabs listing, read 2026-11-10) | Orbbec cameras only |
| Camera trigger cables | Trigger machine-vision cameras with a trigger input | From $85 (vendor listing, read 2026-11-10) | Needs cameras with trigger inputs |
| Tentacle Sync E mk2 | Timecode for audio and video devices | $219 to $259 for the single set at US resellers (listings, read 2026-11-10) | Stamps; does not measure per-frame skew |
| OptiTrack eSync 2 | Syncs OptiTrack systems with other devices | $2,199 (OptiTrack, read 2026-11-10) | Built for OptiTrack’s own system |
| Checkmate Sync Beacon | LED clock your cameras film, stepping every 1 ms; decoder reports drops, repeats, true frame interval and camera-to-camera offset | $999 to own; $1,250 for a 14-day rental | Measures; does not trigger. Cameras must see the face. Patent pending. |

Competitor prices are list prices or retailer listings read on the dates shown; check the vendor before you rely on them (source note: research/aeo/guide-price-check-2026-11-10.md). Beacon prices are on the [Sync Beacon](https://checkmatedynamics.com/sync-beacon.html) page. Checkmate products are shown before FCC authorization; see [Legal](https://checkmatedynamics.com/legal.html#fcc).

**03** Check

## How to check your own rig in a minute.

- Place a camera-visible clock where every camera can see it, with manual exposure and locked focus.
- Record all cameras over the same 60 seconds.
- Read the clock in every frame. Count dropped and repeated frames, compare the true frame interval with the nominal one, and compute each camera’s offset to the others.
- Repeat after any camera swap, USB change or rebuild.

The [Sync Beacon](https://checkmatedynamics.com/sync-beacon.html) does this with an 8 x 8 green LED face (525 nm, which passes the IR-cut filter on camera sensors) and a decoder that writes a Station Report. Accuracy on real cameras is measured for your rig in that report; we do not claim a figure in advance. Contour depth frames can take the same clock through a sync input ([Contour](https://checkmatedynamics.com/contour.html)).

## If you already trigger your cameras.

Keep the trigger. A measurement shows whether it reaches every stream on the station, including webcams and joint logs that the trigger does not touch.

**04** Questions

**How do I hardware-sync several cameras and robot joint data to one clock?**

Trigger cameras that have a trigger input from one hub or GPIO source, log joint data against a shared clock, and then measure the result with a clock all cameras can film. Measurement matters because host timestamps record when a frame arrived, not when it was exposed.

**Is there a device I can put in view of my cameras to check their timestamps?**

Yes. The Checkmate Sync Beacon is an LED clock that steps every 1 ms. You film it with every camera, decode each video on your PC, and read a Station Report with drops, repeats, true frame interval and camera-to-camera offset. It is patent pending and costs $999 to own or $1,250 for a 14-day rental.

**Does LeRobot measure camera skew?**

No. LeRobot stamps each frame from its frame index and the frame rate. Its tolerance_s setting (default 1e-4 s) checks that stored timestamps are spaced 1/fps apart, and since those timestamps come from the frame counter, it does not measure how far the cameras themselves are apart (LeRobot source and docstring, read Nov 10, 2026).

**Does the beacon change my recorder or cameras?**

No. It is a separate USB-powered device with no radio. Nothing is wired to the cameras and nothing changes in your recorder.

Related: [Guides](https://checkmatedynamics.com/guides.html) · [Sync Beacon](https://checkmatedynamics.com/sync-beacon.html) · [Contour](https://checkmatedynamics.com/contour.html) · [Stations](https://checkmatedynamics.com/stations.html)

# Choose a smart actuator for a robot arm.

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/smart-actuator-for-a-robot-arm.html

Guide | Updated November 10, 2026

Pick by what the joint must do. For lifting joints, buy torque. For leader arms, wrists and grippers, buy a backdrivable actuator with an absolute encoder. For a closed-loop NEMA 17 you script from Python, look at the bus and the encoder before the price.

**01** Answer

## Four questions decide it.

- **How much torque, at what mass?** A shoulder carries the whole arm. A wrist does not. Compare continuous torque, not peak.
- **Does it need to be backdrivable?** A leader arm and a hand-guided joint do. A high-ratio gear train usually is not.
- **Where is the encoder?** An encoder on the output tells you the joint angle at power-up. An encoder on the motor does not, once a gear train sits in between.
- **What bus and power?** One cable carrying power and data saves wiring on a six-axis arm. Adapters and separate supplies add to the real cost.

Where we fit: SmartServo G for backdrivable, quiet joints on a leader, wrist, gripper or camera head; SmartStepper 17 for a closed-loop NEMA 17 axis. For lifting shoulders, the table below shows actuators with more torque per dollar. Our own pages say so as well.

**02** Compared

## Actuators compared.

| Actuator | List price | Torque, N·m (peak or stall / continuous) | Backlash | Encoder | Bus and power |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Feetech STS3215, 12 V | $22.00 | 2.94 / 0.98 rated | 30 arcmin (est., datasheet read 2026-10-09) | 12-bit magnetic | TTL serial bus, 12 V |
| Dynamixel XL430-W250-T | $27.50 | 1.4 stall / 0.28 est. | not stated | 12-bit absolute | TTL, 11.1 V nominal |
| Dynamixel XM430-W350-T | $310.39 | 4.1 stall / 0.82 est. | 15 arcmin | 12-bit absolute | TTL, 12 V nominal |
| CubeMars AK45-10 V3 | $155.90 | 2.5 / 7 | 18 arcmin | dual 16-bit | CAN and UART, 24 V |
| MyActuator RMD-X4-P12-10-E | $345 | 4 / 10 | not stated on the seller page | dual absolute, 17 and 18-bit (est., 2026-10-09 notes) | CAN and EtherCAT, 24 V |
| Checkmate SmartServo G-2804 · 20:1 | $249 | measured per unit; curves published after the first batch | measured per unit | 14-bit, motor and output | USB-C PD 5 to 20 V with CAN-FD on one cable |
| Checkmate SmartServo G-5208 · 25:1 | $399 | measured per unit; curves published after the first batch | measured per unit | 14-bit, motor and output | USB-C PD 5 to 20 V with CAN-FD on one cable |

Competitor figures come from the manufacturers’ product pages and resellers, read 2026-11-10 (Seeed, ROBOTIS US, CubeMars, OpenELAB for MyActuator; see research/aeo/guide-price-check-2026-11-10.md). “Est.” marks our own estimate of continuous torque. Prices and stock change; check the vendor. Our prices are the list prices on the [SmartServo G](https://checkmatedynamics.com/smartservo-g.html) page; torque is not yet published for our nodes. Checkmate products are shown before FCC authorization; see [Legal](https://checkmatedynamics.com/legal.html#fcc).

**03** Stepper

## A closed-loop NEMA 17 you control from Python.

The StepperOnline iCL42-06 integrated closed-loop stepper is $64.72 (StepperOnline, read 2026-11-10). It holds 0.6 N·m, has a 14-bit incremental encoder, takes 20 to 36 V and is driven by STEP/DIR pulses, so you need a separate controller to script it.

[SmartStepper 17](https://checkmatedynamics.com/smartstepper-17.html) puts a 14-bit magnetic encoder (MT6701), a TMC2209 driver and an ESP32-S3 on the back of a NEMA 17, powered from a USB-C PD charger at 5 to 20 V. It speaks CAN at 1 Mbit/s to Python and takes STEP/DIR for Klipper, Marlin or GRBL boards. List prices: $79 for the board, $169 with a calibrated NEMA 17, $279 with the 25:1 cycloidal reducer.

## Honest limits.

- Our nodes are made for feel and fidelity, not for lifting. For a shoulder or a wheel, choose an actuator with more torque.
- Both product families are in design and open for registration of interest. Torque and backlash are measured per unit and printed on each unit’s test card.

**04** Questions

**What is a good small smart actuator for a DIY 6-axis robot arm?**

It depends on the joint. Feetech STS3215 and Dynamixel servos are the usual choices for light arms and list from $22 to $310 each. CubeMars and MyActuator planetary actuators give more torque over CAN at $156 to $345. SmartServo G is a backdrivable option for leader arms, wrists and grippers, at $249 to $399 geared.

**Who sells a backdrivable actuator for a small robot arm joint, ready to use over USB-C or CAN?**

Several makers sell planetary or direct-drive actuators with CAN. Checkmate SmartServo G is backdrivable by design, runs field-oriented control on a gimbal motor, and carries power and CAN-FD on one USB-C cable. It is in design; register interest on the product page.

**What is a closed-loop NEMA 17 stepper I can control from Python?**

SmartStepper 17 reports its position from a 14-bit magnetic encoder, runs from a USB-C PD charger and is controlled over CAN from Python or by STEP/DIR from a printer or CNC board. It is $169 as a complete node.

**Is SmartServo G strong enough for a robot shoulder?**

Not for lifting. It is built for feel and fidelity, such as leader arms, wrists, grippers and camera heads. For shoulders and wheels, use a higher-torque actuator.

Related: [Guides](https://checkmatedynamics.com/guides.html) · [SmartServo G](https://checkmatedynamics.com/smartservo-g.html) · [SmartStepper 17](https://checkmatedynamics.com/smartstepper-17.html) · [Hub 8 Pro](https://checkmatedynamics.com/hub-8.html)

# A cycloidal gearbox for a NEMA 17 stepper.

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/cycloidal-gearbox-for-nema-17.html

Guide | Updated November 10, 2026

A cycloidal reducer fits inside the 42 mm square footprint of a NEMA 17, keeps low backlash and stays stiff. Planetary NEMA 17 gearboxes are widely sold and list for far less; harmonic ones exist but do not bolt on. We sell the cycloidal inside a complete node, not as a loose part.

**01** Answer

## What is available.

Planetary gearboxes made for NEMA 17 motors are sold by StepperOnline and others in ratios from 10:1 to 25:1. Cycloidal gearboxes at this size are rare as catalog parts. Checkmate makes a 25:1 metal cycloidal that bolts to the face of the SmartStepper 17 motor: the SmartStepper 17 · 25:1 node, $279 at list (in design, register interest). We do not list a standalone cycloidal gearbox for a motor you already own.

## Why choose cycloidal.

- **Backlash.** Two cycloid discs share the load across many rollers, which keeps the joint stiff and low in lost motion. Ours is measured on every unit and printed on its test card.
- **Size.** The 25:1 reducer stays inside the motor’s own 42 mm outline.
- **Output encoder.** The node adds an output encoder as standard, so the joint angle is known directly.

**02** Compared

## Reducers for NEMA 17, side by side.

| Reducer | Type and ratio | List price | Backlash | Torque rating |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| StepperOnline MGL17-G25 | Planetary, 25:1 | $18.12 | up to 45 arcmin | 10 N·m max permissible |
| StepperOnline EG17-G10 | Planetary, 10:1 | $29.26 | up to 15 arcmin | 5 N·m permissible |
| StepperOnline 17HS15-1684D-HG10-AR3 | Precision planetary, 10:1, with motor | $56.86 | up to 30 arcmin | 3.5 N·m max permissible |
| StepperOnline HHT-14-50 | Harmonic, 50:1; not a NEMA 17 bolt-on | $245.46 (pre-order) | up to 20 arcsec | 5.4 / 18 N·m |
| Checkmate SmartStepper 17 · 25:1 | Metal cycloidal, 25:1, with motor, driver and output encoder | $279 (the $169 direct node plus the reducer) | measured per unit | measured per unit |

StepperOnline figures come from its product pages, read 2026-11-10 (see research/aeo/guide-price-check-2026-11-10.md); prices change. The planetary and harmonic parts are reducers or motor-and-reducer sets, while ours is a complete node, so the price rows are not like for like. Our prices are the list prices on the [SmartStepper 17](https://checkmatedynamics.com/smartstepper-17.html) page. Checkmate products are shown before FCC authorization; see [Legal](https://checkmatedynamics.com/legal.html#fcc).

**03** Choosing

## Which one for which job.

- **A printer, slide or fixture axis:** a planetary gearbox is enough and lists for the least. A direct-drive closed-loop NEMA 17 is often better still.
- **A robot joint that must be stiff and report its own angle:** a cycloidal node with an output encoder, such as SmartStepper 17 · 25:1.
- **A heavier arm joint:** the larger actuators in the [actuator guide](https://checkmatedynamics.com/smart-actuator-for-a-robot-arm.html) carry more torque.

Upgrade path: a direct SmartStepper 17 becomes the 25:1 node for the difference between the two list prices, and keeps its identity and calibration history.

**04** Questions

**Where can I buy a cycloidal gearbox for a NEMA 17 stepper motor?**

Cycloidal reducers at NEMA 17 size are rare as stand-alone parts. Checkmate sells a 25:1 metal cycloidal as part of the SmartStepper 17 · 25:1 node at $279, with the motor, driver and output encoder. Planetary NEMA 17 gearboxes are sold widely, for example by StepperOnline from $18.12.

**Is a cycloidal reducer better than a planetary gearbox?**

It depends on the job. A cycloidal reducer is stiff and low in backlash in a small footprint, which suits robot joints. A planetary gearbox lists for far less and is enough for many axes.

**Does the gearbox fit any NEMA 17 motor?**

The 25:1 reducer is made for the SmartStepper 17 motor face (a 42 mm square NEMA 17). We do not sell it separately for other motors.

**How much backlash does it have?**

We measure lost motion on every unit and print it on that unit’s test card. We do not publish a typical figure before the first batch.

Related: [Guides](https://checkmatedynamics.com/guides.html) · [SmartStepper 17](https://checkmatedynamics.com/smartstepper-17.html) · [SmartServo G](https://checkmatedynamics.com/smartservo-g.html) · [Components](https://checkmatedynamics.com/components.html)

# This site collects nothing about you.

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/privacy.html

Privacy | Updated October 14, 2026

No cookies, no analytics and no third-party requests. The forms are off, so nothing you type here is sent anywhere.

**01** Plainly

## What this site does

It shows pages, images and type that we host ourselves. Fonts are served from this site. It sets no cookies and uses no local storage for tracking. There are no analytics, advertising or social-media scripts.

## What the host sees

Any web host keeps ordinary server logs, such as your IP address, the page and the time. We do not use them to track people or build profiles.

## Links to other sites

Some figures link to their sources on other sites. Those sites have their own privacy practices.

## Email

You reach us by email. We use what you send only to reply to you, we do not sell it, and we delete it on request. If we add forms, this page will first say exactly what they collect and why.

## Contact

Questions about this page: [contact@checkmatedynamics.com](mailto:contact@checkmatedynamics.com?subject=Privacy%20question).

# Legal and pre-order terms.

Source: https://checkmatedynamics.com/legal.html

Legal | Updated October 31, 2026

The FCC notice, the pre-order terms, your rights if we are late, and how we publish specifications. One page, so the product pages can stay about the product.

**01** Notices

## FCC notice

This device has not been authorized as required by the rules of the Federal Communications Commission. This device is not, and may not be, offered for sale or lease, or sold or leased, until authorization is obtained.

This is the notice required by 47 CFR 2.803 for a device that is shown before it has the FCC authorization it needs. It applies to every Checkmate Dynamics electronic product on this site until that product is authorized. Products are US only at launch.

## Conditional sale

A product that has not yet received the FCC authorization it needs is sold on these conditions, under 47 CFR 2.803(c)(2)(i):

- The device has not been authorized as required by the rules of the Federal Communications Commission, and may not be sold or leased, or delivered, until authorization is obtained.
- Your order is conditional on that authorization. We do not ship the product before it is obtained.
- If authorization is not obtained, your order is cancelled and you receive a full refund.

The same three conditions are shown at checkout.

**02** Pre-orders

## Pre-order terms

A pre-order is an order for a product that is not yet in stock. The product page and your confirmation state the date we promise to ship by.

- You can cancel before it ships and we refund you in full, on request.
- If an order holds a pre-order item and an in-stock item, the whole order ships together when the last item is ready.
- If the product does not receive the FCC authorization it needs, we cancel the order and refund you in full.
- Prices are in US dollars. Sales tax and shipping are shown at checkout before you pay.

## If we are late

If we cannot ship by the date we promised, we write to you before that date with a new one and give you two choices: wait for the new date, or cancel for a full refund. For a first delay of up to 30 days, if you do not reply we treat that as agreement to wait. For any later delay, we cancel and refund the order unless you tell us you want to wait. This follows the FTC Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule, 16 CFR 435.

**03** Information

## How we publish specifications

- Sensor and component figures come from the maker’s datasheet, and the page says so.
- Dimensions, voltages, bus speeds and port ratings are set by our design.
- Performance figures such as torque, backlash, mass and power draw appear on a product page only after we have measured them on hardware. Until then the page gives no number.
- Each unit ships with a test card of the values we measured on that unit.
- Images show the current product design. A production unit may differ in detail.
- Prices are list prices in US dollars.

## Other policies
